summary: Keeps fresh Linux Docker Compose development startup writable when the host checkout owner differs from the container's default node user.
userImpact: Linux developers can start a fresh checkout with pnpm run dev or bash dev.sh without TypeScript failing to write generated workspace files.
configuration: On Linux, dev.sh passes the caller's numeric UID and GID to the development backend image and service; EG_DEV_UID and EG_DEV_GID remain optional overrides.
The development backend uses a writable temporary home for host-matched Linux identities. Production images and Compose configuration are unchanged.

notes: No database schema or data changes are required.

security: Development startup matches the host checkout owner instead of broadening source permissions or running the container as root by default; production container identity is unchanged.
documentation: The generated technical release notes describe the Linux development startup correction and CI cold-start qualification.
rollback: Revert to the previous development Compose and Dockerfile definition; no database rollback is needed.
validation: A fresh disposable development Compose stack started locally with pnpm run dev --wait --wait-timeout 900; backend /ready and frontend / returned HTTP 200.
The change-selected CI lane runs the same development entry point on a fresh Linux runner and requires healthy endpoints without a redundant dependency installation.
